attestation.scopeStatement: This artifact attests completion of the mission arc represented by this session and anchors continuity for future AI instances operating under the same policy realm.

brainDump.summary: Session started as an AFP rendering-quality effort and evolved into a full operating model: strict/native rendering focus, structured workstreams, governance automation, rollback/version discipline, issue logging, workbook-safe update strategy, three-realm architecture (policy/management/product), SQL-backed state + reasoning + knowledge synchronization, and environment-first controls with persistent PM console checks.
timelineNarrative: Initial phases focused on AFP output parity and strict styling mode while preserving inferred mode as an option.
Work shifted to deeper renderer accuracy: AFP object/font/overlay handling, diagnostics expansion, and print-centric interpretation strategy proposals.
Project plan governance matured: phased delivery, recurring next-step execution from plan, documentation updates as mandatory build behavior.
Spreadsheet integrity became a recurring incident stream: corruption diagnosis, non-destructive update constraints, backup/restore discipline, and metadata parity checks were introduced.
Policy hardening was introduced: AI-POLICY as living operational contract, then explicit human-only control over critical wording and governance clauses.
Issues log and governance event mechanisms were operationalized so troubleshooting and decisions are preserved as first-class artifacts.
Versioning and rollback were formalized with checkpoint tooling and process gates to avoid destructive drift and support restoration.
Boilerplate promotion model matured: sync candidates, update package rollups, manifest/checklist artifacts, and transfer-ready payloads.
Database-centric management expanded: project/boilerplate realm databases, reasoning/experience stores, identifier registries, and action pipelines.
Workspace architecture transitioned from legacy naming to three canonical realms: policy (framework/governance), management (PM tooling/state/docs), product (application deliverable).
Workstream H executed migration mechanics: folder moves, compatibility symlinks, settings/build path rewrites, guardrail updates, SQL token migration, and report/security config normalization.
Gate failures were resolved iteratively: CI artifact index requirements, managed-tooling guard behavior during move states, realm-name test assumptions, and product fidelity path handling.
Final validation reached full quality gate success with canonical realm structure and environment checks passing.
notableEngineeringOutcomes: Environment-first enforcement became explicit (console liveness/visibility checks integrated in build lifecycle).
Cross-realm traceability and policy sync reports now act as governance evidence.
Quality gates now enforce policy linting, artifact completeness, managed tooling discipline, and realm boundaries.
Python and Java PM tooling coexistence was normalized under management realm conventions.
Fidelity gate behavior now gracefully handles absent corpus assets in cleaned environments.
leadDeveloperIntentForFutureSessions: Preserve realm boundaries: policy defines operating model, management drives process/state, product delivers application behavior.
Prefer smallest-change biggest-gain increments while keeping all governance evidence machine-verifiable.
Treat identifiers as durable records across code, governance, and project management domains.
Maintain workbook updates via controlled tooling only; avoid destructive round-trip rewrites.
Any major process mutation should emit an issue/governance record and remain human-steerable.
